classification.difficultyReason: Read each vertex and y-intercept, form a vertex-form equation and substitute the intercept to determine its leading coefficient.

content.prompt: Find the equations of the quadratic functions sketched below.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with vertex (1,1), y-intercept 3, positive axis arrows and arrows at both curve ends; no grid or additional numeric ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: The equation is omitted from the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The vertex gives $y=a(x-1)^2+1$. Substitute the $y$-intercept $(0,3)$:
$$\begin{align*}3&=a(0-1)^2+1\\3&=a+1\\a&=2\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=2(x-1)^2+1$.

spec.description: Downward-opening parabola with vertex (3,2), y-intercept -7 and two unlabelled x-intercepts. Positive axis ends and both curve ends have arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: The equation and x-intercept values are omitted.

answer.worked:
The vertex gives $y=a(x-3)^2+2$. Substitute the $y$-intercept $(0,-7)$:
$$\begin{align*}-7&=a(0-3)^2+2\\-7&=9a+2\\-9&=9a\\a&=-1\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=-(x-3)^2+2$.

spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with vertex (-2,-4), y-intercept -2 and two unlabelled x-intercepts. Positive axis ends and both curve ends have arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: The equation and x-intercept values are omitted.

answer.worked:
The vertex gives $y=a(x+2)^2-4$. Substitute the $y$-intercept $(0,-2)$:
$$\begin{align*}-2&=a(0+2)^2-4\\-2&=4a-4\\2&=4a\\a&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=\frac12(x+2)^2-4$.

spec.description: Downward-opening parabola with vertex (-1,4), y-intercept 1 and two unlabelled x-intercepts. Positive axis ends and both curve ends have arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: The equation and x-intercept values are omitted.

answer.worked:
The vertex gives $y=a(x+1)^2+4$. Substitute the $y$-intercept $(0,1)$:
$$\begin{align*}1&=a(0+1)^2+4\\1&=a+4\\a&=-3\end{align*}$$
Hence $y=-3(x+1)^2+4$.
